issues: Hero title only fills about 60% of the desktop width. Its height was capped by a 1fr grid row inside a fixed 100vh hero, so 'typography IS the image' fell short and the hero read like a normal headline.
Opacity-0 scroll reveals left whole sections blank when the IntersectionObserver never fired (story on Birth Bear, CTA on catalog). The page showed large empty off-white and red slabs.
Mobile category word-marks broke mid-word (BOKSHANDSC/HOENEN, PROTECTIE/B/ESCHERMING, OEFENWAPEN/S) because of overflow-wrap:anywhere.
The second (black) marquee band sat almost entirely behind the red one. Only slivers showed, so the crossed-tape effect was lost.
The pinned product rail sat on plain off-white with tiny cards. The signature section had no colour block and little visual weight, which left the 'bold primary-colour blocks' brief unmet.
With only two products (Birth Bear), the rail still pinned for a tiny horizontal distance, leaving dead scroll space.
The rail track did not react to scroll velocity, unlike the marquees, so the kinetic language was inconsistent.
fixed: Hero is now min-height instead of a fixed height. The title is fitted against 60% of the viewport height instead of the leftover grid row, so the condensed face spreads across the full width.
Reveals are transform-only (slide plus slight tilt) in template and catalog. Content can never be invisible, but the kinetic entrance stays.
Category names stay on one line and are fitted by JS to their column, shrinking only when needed. No more mid-word breaks on mobile.
Marquee bands are now offset and crossed (black +3.2deg high, primary -3deg low with a hard black drop shadow). Both tapes read as a deliberate X.

The product rail is now a full primary-colour block. It has a giant outlined ghost word-mark (product count or brand name) behind the cards, bigger cards, a black 'Alles bekijken' disc and an on-primary progress bar.
The rail only pins when the horizontal overflow is at least 30% of the viewport. Otherwise it falls back to a native swipe strip.
The rail track now skews with scroll velocity, the same as the marquee bands and word-marks.
